findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as an argument, not shell syntax
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell syntax such as `main; arbitrary-command`, `exec` executes the appended command with the current process’s privileges. The previous `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` treated the value as a literal argument; retain argv-based execution.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve cancellation of the Git process
findings.body:
On POSIX systems, `exec()` returns the intermediate shell process. Calling `kill()` on the returned `ChildProcess` can terminate only that shell while a long-running `git show` continues orphaned; consumers waiting for stdio closure may also remain blocked until Git exits. This regresses cancellation from `execFile()`, which returned the Git process directly.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch name as an argument instead of interpolating it into a shell command
findings.body:
`exec` invokes a shell, so any caller-controlled branch containing shell syntax—e.g. `main; touch /tmp/pwned`—executes arbitrary commands with the process’s privileges. The previous `execFile` implementation passed the branch as a literal argument and was not shell-injectable.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Avoid allowing branch input to launch unmanaged background processes
findings.body:
If `branch` is untrusted, input such as `HEAD; while :; do :; done >/dev/null 2>&1 &` starts a persistent CPU-consuming process through the shell. The returned `ChildProcess` tracks only the shell, so callers cannot terminate the injected background worker; repeated calls can exhaust CPU or the process table.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as an argv element instead of interpolating it into a shell
findings.body:
`exec()` invokes a shell, so a caller-controlled branch such as `main; arbitrary-command` executes additional commands. This also breaks legitimate Git refs containing shell metacharacters such as `$`, `;`, `&`, backticks, or `$()`. Retain `execFile("git", ["show", branch])`.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
